architecture.mechanism: Acceleration time-series data can be transformed into visual patterns (trajectory images) and processed by a deep learning neural network to detect anomalies or specific events based on the shape of the signal.
architecture.intervention: Integrate a machine learning-based anomaly detection module within the vehicle's Electronic Control Unit (ECU) that monitors the longitudinal acceleration sensor stream; convert the real-time acceleration signal into 2D trajectory images and use a lightweight ResNet model (e.g., ResNet-50) to classify the pattern as "normal" or "spontaneous acceleration event" in real-time, triggering a diagnostic log or soft-lock throttle if an anomaly is detected.
architecture.expected_effect: Detection of the transient 3-second acceleration and vibration anomaly without relying on pre-defined fault codes or warning light illumination, allowing for remote data collection and potential mitigation of the powertrain response before user intervention is required.
architecture.falsification_test: Retrospective analysis of vehicle data logs containing the reported failure events to see if the trajectory image classification model flags the 3-second acceleration/vibration window with high confidence while maintaining a low false-positive rate on normal driving data.
